newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold ends down on last-minute selling.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends down on last-minute selling.

text.p: Hong Kong gold dropped steeply on European selling just before the local market closed and ended below New York's previous close, bullion dealers said on Wednesday.
"The morning was very quiet, but suddenly in the afternoon we got sell orders from London," said one bullion trader.
Gold dealers said the sales were profit-taking from Europe after gold rose steadily in Asian trading hours.
Bullion ended at US$353.50/354 an ounce against New York's US$354.00/50 close on Tuesday.
Spot gold prices remained tightly range-bound, bouncing between $354.20 and $354.70, with buying interest on the bottom and interest to sell at the top of the range, dealers said.
Physical gold demand had dropped off slightly, some traders said.
Bullion dealers saw the short-term range between $352 and $354.
Local gold ended HK$14 higher at HK$3,271 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +5.00 from its previous fix at nil.
